headline: Machado is home after seven tries. No election is set.
summary: María Corina Machado walked into a church in Lara state on Sunday, ten months after she fled by speedboat to collect her Nobel Peace Prize. Her party says she tried to come back seven times. US forces took Maduro in January. The acting president got 90 days, has stayed on and set no election. Trump said he knew nothing about it.
cover_answer: Nobody admits blocking her. This time she got through.
table_question: If the referee is on the other team, do you still play the game?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: María Corina Machado went home to Venezuela on Sunday after ten months away. The people running her country wouldn't let her run against them, so she hid, then left on a boat at night. She walked into a church and everyone there hugged her, like a whole team when the bus gets back. She's home, and her friends are with her.
5-7.why: A homecoming is the whole story at this age. The hugs carry it; the why stays small.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them the church and the hugs and keeps the hiding to one clause. The boat at night is the concrete anchor; the politics go to the Try answer. Expect "is she safe now?" Trump said he hopes so. Nobody knows, and that is the honest answer.

8-12.script: Machado won her side's primary in 2023 with over 90% of the vote. The government barred her, so her ally González ran, and credible evidence shows he won 2-to-1, the AP says. The ruling party's vote council named Maduro the winner anyway. A spelling bee judged by one kid's dad.
8-12.why: Primary, ban, stand-in, a count nobody saw.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether the adults keep them, so the script hands over the chain in order: she won, got barred, her stand-in won, the count said otherwise. The judge who is one kid's dad is the mechanism. Expect "why didn't anyone stop them?" The US did, in January. Then it picked the next president itself.

13-17.script: Is Venezuela freer than a year ago? Maduro is in a New York jail, and Machado walked into a church to chants of "Freedom!" But the acting president the US backed got 90 days, has stayed past them and called no election. Who gets to say when the next one is held?
13-17.why: Maduro gone, no election set. Then who decides.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: the strongman is gone and no one has been elected. The script asks who gets to set the date, which the AP leaves open: Machado wants one now, the US says stabilise the economy first. Expect "so was removing Maduro good or bad?" Say what you think, then show them the 90 days.

5-7.q: Why did she have to hide?
5-7.a: The bosses wouldn't let her run against them. She hid for almost a year, then left by boat.

8-12.a: Her team says seven tries were blocked. Venezuela and the US deny it.
Delcy Rodríguez, Maduro's old deputy, with US backing. No election is set.

13-17.q: Why does the US get a say at all?
13-17.a: Its military took Maduro in January and backed Rodríguez to replace him.

13-17.q: Did she really give Trump her Nobel Prize?
13-17.a: Yes, at the White House in January. The committee says it can't move.
